Petrus Plancius
pā'trūs plän'sī-ūs
n. (Petrus Plancius, 1552–1622, Flemish Reformed minister at Amsterdam, cartographer and astronomer, a leading Counter-Remonstrant)
Latinized from Flemish Platevoet; Petrus, from Greek Petros, a stone.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Petrus Plancius fled the Spanish persecution in Brussels disguised as a soldier and settled at Amsterdam, where he served as a minister for thirty-seven years and became the sharpest of the Counter-Remonstrant preachers. He was also, improbably, one of the great cartographers of the age: he drew the charts that carried the first Dutch fleets to the East Indies, taught navigation to their pilots, named constellations of the southern sky, and argued for a northern passage to Asia. The two vocations were one in his mind. He pressed the Dutch East India Company to carry ministers with its merchants, and the earliest Reformed missions in the Indies grew from his insistence. Psa 2:8 was his kind of text: “Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession.” So was Mar 16:15, “Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature.” He opposed Arminius at every turn, and lived to see Dort vindicate the doctrine he had defended.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines a chart as a hydrographical or marine map, for the use of navigators; and to navigate, as to pass on water in ships.

expand to see more

CH'ART, n. A hydrographical or marine map; a draught or projection of some part of the earth's superficies on paper, with the coasts, isles, rocks, banks, channels, and the like.

NAV'IGATE, v.i. To pass on water in ships; to sail.

COS'MOGRAPHY, n. A description of the world or universe.

Key Scripture

Psa 2:8 — "Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession."

Mar 16:15 — "And he said unto them, Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature."

Psa 96:3 — "Declare his glory among the heathen, his wonders among all people."

Act 1:8 — "But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth."

Modern Corruption

The man who charted the sea lanes wanted ministers on the ships, which is the right order of priorities for any commerce.

expand to see more

Plancius is a rebuke to the modern separation of callings. He did not treat cartography as a secular trade pursued alongside a sacred ministry; he drew the maps so that the gospel could travel the routes. Act 1:8 sets the geography of the church's obligation, extending “unto the uttermost part of the earth,” and a man who knows where the uttermost parts are has an advantage in obeying it. Christian engagement with trade, science and navigation is not a distraction from missions; mishandled it becomes one, but rightly handled it is the road.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that Psa 96:3 commands the declaring of God's glory “among the heathen” as a positive duty laid on the church, and that merchants, sailors and mapmakers in a Christian nation are under it as much as ministers. The Dutch companies largely failed at this; Plancius saw the failure coming and said so.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew goy (H1471), nation, heathen; 'erets (H776), earth; Greek ktisis (G2937), creature.

expand to see more

Hebrew goy (H1471) — a nation, the heathen; Psalm 2:8.

Hebrew 'erets (H776) — the earth, land; Psalm 2:8.

Hebrew caphar (H5608) — to recount, to declare; Psalm 96:3.

Greek ktisis (G2937) — creature, creation; Mark 16:15.

Greek eschatos (G2078) — uttermost, last; Acts 1:8.

Usage

"“the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession” (Psa 2:8) — the charted world as inheritance."

"“Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature” (Mar 16:15) — the commission the fleets ignored."

"“Declare his glory among the heathen” (Psa 96:3) — the duty of a trading nation."
